solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leaves suddenly to study intensively in case of sickness

indicators.note: 'in' tells us one piece sits inside the other
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: to cram is to study hard just before an exam

explanation.surface: Someone abandons revision to look up cures because they are feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of sickness' gives S and S, its outer letters, and 'in' places CRAM between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To scram is slang for to go away in a hurry, so it matches leaving suddenly.

clue.text: Crooked smile 'cos of grammatical error

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lopsided smile is blamed on a slip in grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' reworks SMILE plus COS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a mistake in grammar or usage, such as a wrong word form.

clue.text: Exposes delights around the East of India

indicators.note: 'around' says the first piece wraps round the second
in a word written left to right the east end is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone discloses the pleasures found in eastern India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the East of India' is its final letter A, which REVELS goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to expose it to view, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Spread margins are poor, lacking investors ultimately

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged
lacking tells us some letters from the pool are left out of the rearrangement
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A business complains its profit margins are thin because investors have pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MARGINS ARE, remove S ('investors ultimately', signalled by 'lacking'), and rearrange the rest ('poor').
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people put on bread, a kind of spread.

clue.text: Cleaner youth gets accepted by showing caution

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A careful young man is taken on as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARLADY is a British term for a woman paid to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady is a cleaning woman, so the noun cleaner fits directly.

clue.text: Sanctimonious setter might be compared to you

definitions.text: Sanctimonious setter might be compared to you

parts.words: Sanctimonious setter might be compared to you
parts.note: the setter, comparing themself with the solver, claims to be more virtuous, an attitude of smug moral superiority

explanation.surface: The crossword setter hints at being more pious than the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thou' is the old form of 'you', so the setter claiming to be holier than you is the smug phrase itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone who acts as though morally superior, which is what sanctimonious means.

clue.text: Artefact found by priest in church

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic, a church
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An ancient object is discovered by a clergyman inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an artefact.

clue.text: First-class runs — quick to dismiss heart attack

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: dismissing the heart of a word means removing its middle letter

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman scores quickly before a bowler gets him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss heart' takes P, the middle letter, out of RAPID to leave RAID; the cricket words of the surface are misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: An air raid is an attack by aircraft on a ground target.

clue.text: People authorised to give the boss a nod

definitions.text: People authorised to give the boss a nod

parts.words: People authorised to give the boss a nod
parts.note: people whose role is simply to nod through whatever their superior says, agreeing every time

explanation.surface: Staff are given permission to approve a manager's decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes men are sycophants who always agree with those in authority.

clue.text: Impossible position now as intuition goes to pieces

indicators.note: going to pieces means falling apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone's instinct fails them just when they are in a hopeless spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to pieces' rearranges NOW AS INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is bad, a hopeless predicament.

clue.text: Be right and circle around city

parts.note: to live is to be or exist

indicators.note: 'around' here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay correct and walk round a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the circle backwards; the city's own name, read as LIVER plus POOL, is a red herring for the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major city in north-west England.

clue.text: Unusually, responds without instruments

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the words lie outside the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: Someone answers oddly with no musical instruments to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, as in the hymn 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'; the answer lies across unusualLY RESponds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyres are ancient stringed instruments, harp-like and U-shaped.

clue.text: Bread man gets a tip docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man gets a smaller gratuity than he expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the P off TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Country that's in a state

parts.note: a territory wholly surrounded by another nation, read as if it were a nation that is upset

explanation.surface: A nation is described as being in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like 'agitated' but means lying inside another country.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory entirely surrounded by a foreign state, like Lesotho within South Africa.

clue.text: South American chain oddly ignored food

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: A South American chain of shops neglects its food offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' drops C, A and N from CHAIN, leaving H and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with fish or vegetables.

clue.text: Reserve hotel centrally located in coast

indicators.note: located in means placed inside the other piece
centrally points to the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hotel set in the middle of a coastal resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes T from the middle of HOTEL, 'located in' SEASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside something is to reserve it for later use.

clue.text: Criticism certain to include being reportedly misled

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside
reportedly tells us the word is to be heard, not spelt

explanation.surface: Being certain you have been deceived leads to criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns TRICKED into the sound-alike TRICT, which SURE has 'to include'; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a severe critical remark, a censure.

clue.text: Always up on lease, showing respect

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A tenant who always pays the lease on time is respectful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EVER into REVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means feeling or showing deep respect.

clue.text: Fixed agreement to drop end of term drink

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or altered, so the letters are rearranged
dropping means losing some letters from the pool
end of points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A settled agreement to give up end-of-term drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AGREEMENT, drop M ('end of term'), then rearrange the rest ('Fixed').
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a drink made from unfermented tea leaves.

clue.text: New resort accepts one should have a ball

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside
new means made afresh, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newly opened resort welcomes everyone who wants fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges RESORT and it 'accepts' I.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, to have a great time.

clue.text: Villain's regret accepting turn about

definitions.note: read as 'villain is', so the definition is a noun

indicators.note: accepting means taking inside
about means turned round, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A villain regrets being won over by a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GO into OG, which RUE is 'accepting'; 'Villain's' means 'Villain is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, a villain.

clue.text: Serious expression from a serious expert

explanation.surface: An expert pulls a grave face.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'serious' tempts a solver to treat it as one idea; one is the definition, the other GRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain.

clue.text: Writes music from the twenties

definitions.meaning: to score a piece is to compose or arrange music
a score is twenty, so twenties in this sense are groups of twenty

explanation.surface: A composer harks back to the music of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring is composing music, and a score is a set of twenty.

clue.text: Fancy striker beginning to attack

parts.note: a chimer is one who strikes bells

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fancy footballer starts to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football but means a bell-ringer, a CHIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or wild fantasy.

clue.text: Buy no better container for lifting tree

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means reading upwards, backwards
the words act as a container, holding the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Advice to buy a better plant pot for raising a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' signals letters held inside buY NO BEtter, and 'for lifting' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical tree prized for its dark wood.

clue.text: I'll be heard after diplomacy — touching?

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other in the answer
heard means the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone promises to speak up after a tactful pause, wondering whether that is touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be heard' turns I'LL into the sound-alike ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to touch, so it fits touching.

clue.text: Proportion of allowance unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Part of an allowance has not been used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last N from RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a proportion between two quantities.

clue.text: Copper delayed after single refusal to give protection

indicators.note: after puts the copper piece behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman arrives late after a flat refusal to protect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to vaccinate, giving protection against disease.

clue.text: Going off beam, taken in by confidence trick

indicators.note: being taken in by something means going inside it

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone loses their way after being fooled by a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off beam' tempts as a single phrase, but 'beam' is RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying means wandering away, going off course.

clue.text: Feel bitter about gifts being unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping strips off the outer layer, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone resents gifts as they open them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being unwrapped' takes P and S off PRESENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it.
